title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-06-06
source: 7 Inch Half Track Reel Master @ 7.5 ips(Recorded By Bear on a Sony 770 Reel 2 Reel)- 1st Generation Cassettes (TDK SAX-100's) Transferred By Dick Latvala(Master Reel Playback on a Technics 1506 Reel 2 Reel-Tascam 122 MK111 Cassette Deck No Dolby); Analog to Digital Transfer(Cassettes played back on Nakamichi Dragon-Sony PCM-R500 DAT @ 44.1KHz by Jim Wise circa late 1990's) Zero Gen DAT play back on a Sony PCM R-500-Digital Out @ 16/44.1kHz-Digital Audio Labs Card deluxe-WAV @ 16/44.1KHz; Editing(Adobe Audition CC)-Mastering & Processing(iZotope Ozone 6)-FLAC encoding(dBpoweramp)-Tagging(Tag & Re-name); Jim Wise

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a relaxed Fillmore West set, highlighted by a smoking Alligator jam and tight Lovelight performance.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised for its crystal‑clear, low‑hiss soundboard quality, making the extended improvisations shine. Musically the band stretches out into unique grooves, with the second half—especially Alligator, Not Fade Away, The Dew and Lovelight—described as smoking and tightly executed. While a few reviewers note the first half is unremarkable, the overall vibe is relaxed and inspired.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high praise for both performance (70% weight) and recording quality (30% weight); minor early‑set criticism does not outweigh the strong positives.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers note a noticeable reduction in hiss, magnificent sound clarity, and overall excellent quality compared to earlier sources.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A relaxed Fillmore West atmosphere lets the band stretch out; early songs are deemed routine, but the second half flows tightly with standout jams and superb drumming.

band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen's organ on Lovelight is likened to Janis Joplin—described as a cosmic male/female power blend.
band_member_comments.Drums: Superb drumming highlighted throughout the performance.
